name: network and transport
owns: everything between the application's bytes and the application: IP, DNS, TLS, HTTP versions, and the stateful transports built on top
why_in_D: Each layer terminates something. A proxy that terminates TLS sees plaintext. A cache that terminates HTTP decides what is fresh. A QUIC implementation that resets a stream has its own idea of when data was delivered. Any disagreement between two terminators about the same message is a smuggling primitive, and smuggling is not an application bug at all.

factors.name: HTTP request line parsing strictness
factors.def: which characters and line endings a parser accepts as a request boundary
factors.observable: differential response between two parsers fed the same raw bytes

factors.name: header folding acceptance
factors.def: whether obsolete line folding is honoured, and by which hop
factors.observable: whether a folded header is joined, dropped or rejected per hop

factors.name: duplicate header resolution
factors.def: which of two headers with the same name wins, and whether all hops agree
factors.observable: differing interpretation of Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding between hops

factors.name: Transfer-Encoding versus Content-Length precedence
factors.def: which framing a hop prefers when both are present
factors.observable: a smuggled prefix that one hop treats as a new request

factors.name: chunk size parsing tolerance
factors.def: whether chunk extensions, whitespace or hex case are tolerated, and asymmetrically
factors.observable: boundary placement differing between two parsers

factors.name: request target normalisation
factors.def: whether the target is normalised before routing, and where
factors.observable: path traversal or route confusion between surface and handler

factors.name: absolute URI acceptance
factors.def: whether a hop accepts an absolute URI in the request target, which can redirect onward routing
factors.observable: routing change when the target becomes absolute

factors.name: connection reuse semantics
factors.def: whether a hop reuses a backend connection across clients, which is where desync persists
factors.observable: a response delivered to the wrong client after a desync

factors.name: keep-alive timeout asymmetry
factors.def: the gap between two hops' idle timers, which decides whether a request lands on a dying connection
factors.observable: a request accepted by one hop after the other closed

factors.name: pipelining support
factors.def: whether a hop queues multiple requests on one connection, giving desync more room
factors.observable: two responses ordered incorrectly after a crafted pair

factors.name: HTTP/2 to HTTP/1 downgrade path
factors.def: how a version mismatch is translated, which is the classic smuggling seam
factors.observable: header or framing change introduced by the translator

factors.name: HTTP/2 pseudo-header validation
factors.def: whether pseudo-headers are validated before use, and whether order and duplication are checked
factors.observable: acceptance of a forbidden pseudo-header combination

factors.name: HTTP/2 header name case handling
factors.def: whether uppercase names are rejected, which decides whether a down-translated request is ambiguous
factors.observable: acceptance and downstream form of an uppercase header

factors.name: HTTP/2 stream concurrency limit
factors.def: the cap on concurrent streams, which is a resource boundary and a desync lever
factors.observable: behaviour when the cap is exceeded by exactly one

factors.name: HTTP/2 reset semantics
factors.def: whether a cancelled stream's data is discarded or still forwarded
factors.observable: backend receiving a body for a stream the client cancelled

factors.name: HPACK dynamic table handling
factors.def: whether a hop maintains state across requests, which makes some compression oracles durable
factors.observable: state carried between requests in the same connection

factors.name: HTTP/3 and QUIC fallback
factors.def: whether a client falls back to TCP when UDP is filtered, and whether the fallback differs in policy
factors.observable: policy difference applicable over UDP versus TCP

factors.name: QUIC connection migration
factors.def: whether a connection survives a change of address, which breaks IP-based controls
factors.observable: session continuing across a source address change

factors.name: QUIC stream reset propagation
factors.def: how a reset is reported to the application, and whether partial data is delivered
factors.observable: partial body accepted after a reset

factors.name: 0-RTT replay window
factors.def: whether early data can be replayed, and what server state that duplication corrupts
factors.observable: a replayed request producing a second effect

factors.name: TLS termination topology
factors.def: where TLS actually ends, which decides which hop sees plaintext and which only ciphertext
factors.observable: which node can read a header in the clear

factors.name: SNI-based routing
factors.def: whether routing depends on the cleartext server name, which can disagree with the Host header
factors.observable: a request routed to one host and served by another

factors.name: certificate name handling
factors.def: whether the presented certificate is checked against the name actually used
factors.observable: acceptance of a mismatched name under some path

factors.name: TLS version and cipher negotiation
factors.def: whether a downgrade is possible, and which policies each hop enforces
factors.observable: negotiated parameters under forced client capability

factors.name: session resumption state
factors.def: whether resumed sessions carry stale authorisation, which is an identity lifetime seam
factors.observable: a permission change not reflected after resumption

factors.name: client certificate forwarding
factors.def: how a client identity is conveyed to the application, and whether it can be forged or stripped
factors.observable: whether a client-supplied header overrides the certificate

factors.name: ALPN negotiation
factors.def: whether protocol selection can be steered to a less strict handler
factors.observable: which handler answers under each ALPN value

factors.name: DNS resolution path
factors.def: which resolver is authoritative, caching TTLs, and where a forged answer can enter
factors.observable: answer divergence between two vantage points

factors.name: DNS rebinding window
factors.def: the TTL and caching behaviour that decides how fast an answer can change under a page's feet
factors.observable: a name resolving differently on a second query

factors.name: DNS response size and truncation
factors.def: whether truncation is honoured or ignored, which affects spoofing feasibility
factors.observable: handling of a truncated response

factors.name: CNAME chain handling
factors.def: whether a chain is followed to the same conclusion by resolver, cache and application
factors.observable: a chain producing different final hosts per hop

factors.name: search domain and suffix behaviour
factors.def: whether a short name expands locally, which is a naming confusion primitive
factors.observable: resolution of a single-label name inside an internal network

factors.name: TTL enforcement consistency
factors.def: whether every cache honours the stated freshness or applies its own minimum
factors.observable: stale content served past the declared TTL

factors.name: cache key composition
factors.def: which request properties are part of the key, which decides what can be poisoned
factors.observable: two requests differing in one property sharing a cache entry

factors.name: cache normalisation of the target
factors.def: whether the cache normalises case, encoding or dot segments before keying
factors.observable: an entry storing a payload under a normalised key

factors.name: unkeyed header acceptance
factors.def: whether a response varies on a header that is not in the key, which is the poisoning mechanism
factors.observable: a response cached with a value derived from an unkeyed input

factors.name: cache invalidation on write
factors.def: whether a write invalidates every representation of the resource
factors.observable: a stale copy served after a successful write

factors.name: proxy versus origin normalisation order
factors.def: what is normalised where, which decides whether a payload reaches the origin intact
factors.observable: a payload altered by one hop and not another

factors.name: hop-by-hop header stripping
factors.def: which headers are removed per hop, and whether an attacker can smuggle one through
factors.observable: arrival of a header that should have been stripped

factors.name: forwarded-address trust chain
factors.def: which hops may set client address headers, which decides identity spoofing and rate limit evasion
factors.observable: acceptance of a spoofed client address from an untrusted path

factors.name: WebSocket upgrade validation
factors.def: whether the upgrade is authenticated and origin-checked, and whether the same checks recur per message
factors.observable: a connection established without the expected check

factors.name: WebSocket origin enforcement
factors.def: whether the Origin header is validated, since browsers do not apply same-origin to sockets
factors.observable: a cross-origin socket accepted

factors.name: WebSocket framing edge cases
factors.def: masking requirements, fragmentation, control frame size limits and their enforcement
factors.observable: acceptance of a frame the specification forbids

factors.name: WebSocket proxy caching
factors.def: whether an intermediary caches socket-adjacent traffic or upgrades incorrectly
factors.observable: a message delivered to a party that never sent it

factors.name: server-sent events reconnect semantics
factors.def: whether a reconnect resumes with Last-Event-ID, and whether that value is trusted
factors.observable: replay or skip of events after a reconnect

factors.name: event stream buffering
factors.def: how intermediaries buffer a streaming response, which decides whether it is live or batched
factors.observable: arrival timing of events through a proxy

factors.name: WebRTC ICE candidate exposure
factors.def: whether local addresses leak, and whether the leak is a data channel or an identity one
factors.observable: candidate list contents from a page

factors.name: WebRTC data channel policy
factors.def: whether data channels bypass origin policy, since they are not subject to CORS
factors.observable: a channel established across origins

factors.name: WebTransport session control
factors.def: whether multiplexed streams share authorisation, and whether one stream can affect another
factors.observable: state change in one stream after another closes

factors.name: TURN and relay trust
factors.def: whether a relay validates who may use it, which is both abuse and an egress path
factors.observable: relay allocation without expected credentials

factors.name: connection pooling tenancy
factors.def: whether a pool shares backend connections across tenants
factors.observable: a response belonging to another tenant

factors.name: rate limit keying
factors.def: what the limiter counts, which decides whether a limit can be sidestepped by changing one property
factors.observable: a limit bypassed by altering a single header or path

factors.name: netflow and log sampling
factors.def: whether an action is visible to the defender, which decides whether a probe is silent
factors.observable: presence of a request in recorded telemetry

factors.name: MTU and fragmentation handling
factors.def: whether oversized or fragmented requests are reassembled consistently per hop
factors.observable: differing reassembly between two parsers

factors.name: TCP urgent pointer handling
factors.def: whether urgent data is stripped, honoured or forwarded, which is an old desync seam
factors.observable: byte stream difference between hops

factors.name: IP option acceptance
factors.def: whether a hop honours source routing or record route options
factors.observable: behaviour with a chosen IP option set

factors.name: proxy protocol trust
factors.def: whether a PROXY header is accepted from an untrusted peer, which forges the client address
factors.observable: acceptance of a PROXY header from a non-proxy peer

factors.name: TLS client hello fingerprint policy
factors.def: whether policy keys on the client hello, which makes transport a discriminator
factors.observable: different handling for two hello fingerprints

factors.name: compression side channel surface
factors.def: whether response compression mixes secret and attacker-controlled content
factors.observable: response length correlated with a guessed secret

factors.name: error page divergence
factors.def: which hop generates an error, since the shape of the error reveals the topology
factors.observable: distinct error bodies per failure point

factors.name: timeout asymmetry across hops
factors.def: the difference in timeout decisions that decides whether one side acts and the other does not
factors.observable: a state change on one side only

factors.name: protocol downgrade on failure
factors.def: whether a failure causes a fallback to a weaker protocol rather than an error
factors.observable: a weaker protocol used after a forced failure
